framing: SAATH is a digital delivery vehicle for culturally-adapted Cognitive Stimulation Therapy (CST) — a named psychosocial intervention with real evidence, not an invented game mechanic.
evidence: Cochrane systematic review of 15 RCTs (718 participants): consistent significant benefit to cognitive function following treatment, over and above medication effects, sustained at follow-up up to three months. (Aguirre, Woods, Spector & Orrell, Ageing Research Reviews, 2013; Cochrane CD005562)
2024 systematic review & meta-analysis of the original 14-session CST protocol: strong evidence of positive treatment effects for global cognition, language and quality of life.
Official guidelines exist for adapting CST to other cultures (Aguirre, Spector & Orrell) — cultural adaptation for NER is a documented methodology, not improvisation.
2025 systematic review on personalisation: personalised activities are associated with greater engagement and adherence.
NICE NG97 recommends offering group cognitive stimulation to people with mild-to-moderate dementia.
honestLimit: CST has evidence. Our digital delivery of it does not yet — that is what a pilot would test.

mapping.label: Familiar Pairs
mapping.cstTheme: Matched to CST's object/word recognition and recall sessions.
mapping.note: Uses approved familiar objects from the household's own pack — personalisation the CST literature links to engagement.

mapping.label: Sound & Sight
mapping.cstTheme: Matched to CST's sensory/sound-based orientation sessions.
mapping.note: Visual-only mode available so hearing loss is never penalised.

mapping.label: Pattern Garden
mapping.cstTheme: Matched to CST's categorisation and sorting sessions.
mapping.note: Shape and contrast only — never colour alone.

mapping.label: My Next Step
mapping.cstTheme: Matched to CST's everyday-life / practical activity sessions.

mapping.label: Together Moment
mapping.cstTheme: Matched to CST's reminiscence and current-affairs discussion sessions.
mapping.note: No score, no streak — a shared conversation, not a graded task. Reminiscence can cause distress (Alzheimer's Society guidance) — exit and content rejection are mandatory.
